import html # Example template (should be defined elsewhere in your codebase) USER_POST_FORMAT = """

{post_heading}

Author: {author_id}

{content}
{labels}
""" def render_blog_post(author_id: str, post_heading: str, content: str, labels: list[str]) -> str: """ Render a safe HTML representation of a blog post. Args: author_id: Identifier of the post's creator. post_heading: Heading/title of the post. content: Main body text of the post. labels: List of tag strings. Returns: A string containing the HTML markup for the post, with all user supplied data properly escaped to prevent XSS or injection attacks. """ # Escape all user provided text safe_author = html.escape(author_id, quote=True) safe_heading = html.escape(post_heading, quote=True) safe_content = html.escape(content, quote=False) # Wrap each label in a and escape it safe_labels = ''.join( f'{html.escape(label, quote=True)}' for label in labels ) # Render the final HTML using the template return USER_POST_FORMAT.format( author_id=safe_author, post_heading=safe_heading, content=safe_content, labels=safe_labels )
